besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses (''n Lang seereis het ... gekos' and 'konings en ryk handelaars het ... betaal').
besluite.rede: Both sides have their own subject and verb, so the AWS 2017 requires the comma, and it also separates the two uses of 'en' for the reader.

besluite.fout: A belief that 'gaan' to other parts of the world is wooden.
besluite.rede: 'Versprei' is the natural verb for a faith reaching new places, matches 'sy geloof versprei' later, and keeps who wanted what unchanged.

besluite.fout: 'van ver in die Ooste gekom' mixes a location preposition with a verb of origin and reads awkwardly.
besluite.rede: 'van ver af uit die Ooste' is the natural expression of origin, says the same thing, and leaves the protected next sentence untouched.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.
besluite.rede: 'hierdie goedere het baie geld gekos' and 'handelaars het 'n groot wins gemaak' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.
besluite.rede: 'Daardie handelaar het dit ... geneem' and 'ander het dit ... gedra' each have their own subject and verb.
Afrikaans 'maak' wins, as the lesson says elsewhere; each trader still earns his own profit, so the meaning is unchanged.

besluite.fout: Reasons that 'apart loop' is a wooden, literal image.
besluite.rede: 'nie los van mekaar gestaan nie' is the natural fixed expression and says exactly the same: the two reasons belonged together.

besluite.fout: ''n reis betaal' is loose; the standard construction is 'vir iets betaal'.
besluite.rede: The king pays for the journey in both versions, and 'vir' matches 'daarvoor betaal' and 'vir 'n lang reis te betaal' in the same lesson.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.
besluite.rede: 'Hy wou sy geloof versprei' and 'hy wou wins maak' each have their own subject and verb.
'help wys hoekom' is natural Afrikaans, and 'verduidelik' is a lateral swap that shifts 'show' towards 'explain'.
'aan kos 'n sterk geur gee' is correct Afrikaans, and rewording a glossary definition without a real fault is a lateral move a language agent should not make.
